rationale: Decomposing the deployment term into its irreversible non-current component is a genuine economic sharpening of the archive's best mechanism (not a rescaling), the two ratio terms are on comparable scales so the funding gate retains bite, and the sign convention is internally consistent — though the non-current-growth leg does overlap the well-known investment/asset-growth anomaly, so any gain must come from the interaction rather than the level.

Testing the untouched contracting half of the cross-section under the same funding-source gate is a legitimate and diagnostically informative complement with a coherent sign, but it inherits the archive's structural weakness of assigning exact zeros to the majority (expanders), so the long-short spread will be driven by a small, potentially unstable liquidating-firm tail and the "harvesting vs. liquidating" reading is economically looser than the expansion case.

Subtracting common dividends from operating cash flow perturbs the gate by roughly one to two percent of assets against an oancf/at term an order of magnitude larger, so this is a near-monotone rescaling of RawSurplusGatedExpansion that will almost certainly reproduce its results, and the framing of dividends as an "unavoidable commitment" reducing quality also cuts against their usual positive quality signal.

This is a mechanical crossbreed of two already-evaluated archive members whose outcome will most likely interpolate between them, and mixing a unit-free SUMRANK scale with a raw dollar-scaled gate reintroduces exactly the tail-dilution/magnitude tension the proposal claims to resolve, so it adds little new economic content beyond a hill-climbing step.

The expression is internally inconsistent with its hypothesis: since TS_RANK is non-negative, the signal is weakly negative everywhere, placing large raisers at their own cash-flow *peaks* in the short leg while trough-raisers are numerically indistinguishable from the mass of non-issuers at zero — the reverse of the stated mechanism, and what remains is close to the known gross-issuance anomaly.

Gross profit/assets is typically several times larger than issuance/assets, so the "surplus" difference collapses to gross profitability and the signal degenerates into asset growth × gross profitability — a well-known quality-growth combination largely spanned by the RMW and CMA legs of the FF5 benchmark — thereby discarding the funding-source mechanism the proposal claims to test.
